claims.label: thm:dictionary
claims.statement: Ordered six-arcs, exact [6,3,4]_q codes, equal-phase CSS states, and the AME property correspond, and IsAME(equalPhaseState C) holds exactly when C is an exact [6,3,4] code.
claims.boundary: The Clebsch/GRS separation certificate covers the displayed AME(6,11) state against all six-point GRS-derived states; it classifies no other non-GRS state.

claims.label: prop:diagonal-multiplier-line
claims.statement: For a linear [2m,m,m+1]_q MDS code the space of diagonal code-to-dual multipliers has dimension zero or one; a nonzero multiplier has full support and is unique up to a unit scalar.
claims.boundary: No computational premise; the statement is proved for every finite field and every exact half-dimensional MDS pair.

claims.label: cor:diagonal-isodual-transversal-group
claims.statement: Over an odd prime field the multiplier nullity determines the exact fixed-party projective transversal logical group of the associated [[2m-1,1,m]]_q code: F_q^2 semidirect SL_2(q) when C is diagonally isodual, and F_q^2 semidirect T otherwise.
claims.boundary: The Lean terminal derives the dichotomy from a structure whose fields assert special linearity, coordinatewise propagation, the block-to-multiplier converse, and the complete translation fiber; those inputs are proved in the manuscript. The converse direction imports the companion paper's rigidity theorem.

claims.label: thm:lu-lc-rigidity
claims.statement: For every prime power q and m at least two, every product-unitary intertwiner between stabilizer AME(2m,q) states is Clifford on each tensor factor.
claims.boundary: Owned and proved in the companion rigidity paper. The declarations listed here are the equal-phase specialization this paper invokes, not the arbitrary-additive theorem.

claims.label: cor:transversal-clifford
claims.statement: Every tensor-product conversion between the associated [[2m-1,1,m]]_q encoders is Clifford on every physical factor and on the logical factor.
claims.boundary: Owned and proved in the companion rigidity paper; present in this closure because the exact-carrier argument uses the encoder conversions directly.

claims.label: lem:pauli-phase-correction
claims.statement: A product-Clifford map of stabilizer label groups can be corrected by a product Pauli so that it carries one state ray to the other.
claims.boundary: Owned by the companion rigidity paper. Only the character-realization ingredient is formalized here: every linear character on a Pauli-label subspace is symplectic pairing with an ambient label.

claims.label: lem:six-arc-self-association
claims.statement: At length six, diagonal isoduality of the code is fixed-label Gale self-association of the six-arc, which holds exactly when the arc lies on a conic.
claims.boundary: The Gale/conic equivalence is a manuscript proof; the certificate replays symbolic Gale identities at q=11,13,101.

claims.label: thm:logical-phase
claims.statement: For an odd-prime-field six-arc the fixed-party logical kernel is SL_2(q) on the conic locus and the diagonal split torus off it.
claims.boundary: The Lean terminal takes four explicit propagation hypotheses as structure fields; the party-moving normalizer clause is a manuscript proof input.

claims.label: thm:lc-pencil
claims.statement: On the admitted non-GRS pencil the degree-eight quotient z classifies projective and monomial-code equivalence over odd finite fields.
claims.boundary: The algebraic quotient is unconditional; the classification terminal names its projectivity, bracket-invariance, and local-Clifford holonomy inputs as structure fields.

claims.label: cor:lu-lc-pencil
claims.statement: Over odd prime fields, two admitted non-GRS pencil states are local-unitary equivalent exactly when they are local-Clifford equivalent, and exactly when their z values agree.
claims.boundary: Restricted to odd prime fields: over extension fields Frobenius is an additional local Clifford and no orbit classification is claimed. Uses the imported rigidity theorem and the imported minimum-support atlas.

claims.label: prop:frobenius-sector-divisors
claims.statement: The twisted pencil's Gale pairing multiplier, its vanishing criterion, sector disjointness, and the equivariance of the pencil coordinates under a field automorphism.
claims.boundary: Scalar algebra only; the full extension-field Clifford orbit classification is not claimed.

claims.label: lem:coset-syndrome-charts
claims.statement: Translated equal-phase states are classified by code cosets, distinct cosets are orthogonal, dual-code phase stabilizers read the translation character, and every syndrome has exactly one minimum representative on each three-party support.
claims.boundary: No computational premise.

claims.label: prop:clebsch-x-syndrome
claims.statement: For the Clebsch [6,3,4]_11 code the twelve conic rays give 120 syndromes with a transitive C_10 x A_5 orbit, and each balanced three-party support carries one minimum X-representative.
claims.boundary: Composes the unconditional syndrome core with the cited Clebsch conic, count, and orbit theorem; the defining arc is nonconic, so the fixed-party logical image is the split torus.

claims.label: rem:clebsch-x-syndrome-boundary
claims.statement: Scope remark separating the syndrome charts from the fixed-input operator-pushing fibres and from the computed party image.
claims.boundary: Remark only; asserts no new result.

claims.label: thm:lu-h3-grs
claims.statement: Every odd good non-GRS H3 reduction is separated from the GRS locus by the rank-four marginal-moment multiplicity.
claims.boundary: Bad and GRS reductions are excluded. The three graph cardinalities are exhaustive native evaluations, and the multiplicity identity and separator inherit the star-count evaluation axiom; the incidence and rank bridges are structure fields.

claims.label: thm:q13-lu
claims.statement: At q=13 the classes z=4 and z=12 are separated by an exact four-copy contraction, hence are inequivalent under arbitrary local unitaries.
claims.boundary: The Lean terminal derives inequivalence from the two certified orbit sums 720/13^9 and 3024/13^9; the certificate exhausts all 720 party permutations.

claims.label: thm:fixed-copy-boundary
claims.statement: For irreducible regular code charts every fixed-copy scalar contraction is generically constant on the pencil, so bounded scalar invariants lose the classification data the operator-valued Weyl atlas retains.
claims.boundary: Conceptual contraction-rank proof; the certificate covers the admitted pencil's rank-drop divisor, not a general statement about all invariants.

claims.label: thm:transport-divisor
claims.statement: The reduced four-copy transport operator drops rank exactly on (z-2)(9z-4), with the two components merging in characteristic seven.
claims.boundary: The cycle-polynomial algebra is unconditional; the determinant expansion, systematic rank bridge, and double-coset orbit counts enter as structure fields backed by the certificates.

claims.label: cor:computed-party-splitting
claims.statement: For the twelve listed rows the realized party-permutation extension splits, with explicit complements.
claims.boundary: Exactly the twelve named rows. The abstract splitting consequences are unconditional once a complement is supplied; the complements are certificate-checked.

claims.label: lem:conic-matchings
claims.statement: For six points on a conic over an odd field the three matching lines are concurrent.
claims.boundary: Manuscript proof; no certificate and no Lean terminal.
